title: Efficient bi-allelic tagging in human induced pluripotent stem cells using CRISPR
protocol: Isolate genomic DNA from the desired cell line for tagging.
Amplify the left and right homology arms from isolated genomic DNA.
Set up two PCR reactions for each homology arm using NEBNext High-Fidelity 2× PCR Master Mix and DNA oligos.
Perform amplification using cycling parameters as specified.
Digest the backbone using the reaction for left homology arm insertion.
Incubate the digestion reaction at 37°C for 1 hour.
Purify the digested backbone using gel extraction.
Use Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean-Up System for purification.
Elute purified products in 50 μL elution buffer.
Check the concentration of each product via NanoDrop.
Set up one Gibson assembly reaction for EGFP donor.
Set up another Gibson assembly reaction for mCherry donor.
Incubate each reaction at 50°C for 1 hour.
Transform Stellar chemically competent cells with 2 μL chilled assembled product.
Perform colony PCR reactions for each donor vector, using 8 or 16 colonies.
Perform amplification using cycling parameters for left homology arm confirmation.
Run the PCR product on an agarose gel and select colonies based on the size of the PCR product.
Culture 3–5 positive colonies in 6 mL LB broth with Ampicillin.
Extract plasmid DNA from cultured colonies using the E.Z.N.A. Plasmid DNA Mini Kit protocol.
Confirm the sequence of left homology arm by Sanger sequencing using primer Sanger-Fs1.
Analyze Sanger sequencing results to confirm the sequence of left homology arm in both EGFP and mCherry donors with Snapgene.
Pick one EGFP donor and one mCherry donor with correct left homology arm sequence for right homology arm insertion.
Prepare digestion reaction for EGFP and mCherry donor vectors with NotI.
Incubate the digestion reaction at 37°C for 1 hour.
Purify the digested vectors using gel extraction and Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean-Up System.
Elute in 50 μL elution buffer.
Check the concentration of each product with NanoDrop.
Repeat steps 6–11 to insert the right homology arm into donor vectors.
Check the sequence of right homology arm using the Sanger sequencing primer Sanger-Rs1.
Make midi-prep for EGFP and mCherry donor vectors with both left and right homology arms using QIAGEN Plasmid Plus Midi Kit.
PCR assemble the sgRNA DNA template.
Set up the PCR assembly reaction as specified in Figure B.
Perform assembly PCR using the cycling parameters provided.
Run 5 μL of the PCR product against a DNA ladder on a 2% Agarose Gel to confirm the correct size of the sgRNA DNA template (about 120 bp).
Set up the in vitro transcription (IVT) reaction as directed, adding components in the specified order.
Mix the reaction components thoroughly.
Centrifuge briefly to collect all drops.
Incubate at 37°C for 2 h.
Add 1 μL of DNase I into the reaction mix after incubation.
Mix by pipetting.
Incubate at 37°C for 15 min.
Dilute 0.5 μL of the IVT product in 10 μL of nuclease-free water.
Mix with RNA loading dye.
Heat the sample at 70°C for 10 min.
Chill on ice.
Run on a 2% Agarose Gel against an RNA Ladder to check integrity.
Adjust the volume of the IVT product to 200 μL with nuclease-free water.
Add 100 μL of Binding Buffer.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting.
Add 300 μL of ethanol (>96%) and mix by pipetting.
Transfer the mixture to the GeneJET RNA Purification Micro Column and centrifuge for 30–60 s at 14,000 × g.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 700 μL Wash Buffer 1 and centrifuge for 30–60 s at 14,000 × g.
Discard the flow-through.
Add 700 μL Wash Buffer 2 and centrifuge for 30–60 s at 14,000 × g.
Discard the flow-through.
Centrifuge the empty purification column for an additional 60 seconds at 14,000 × g to completely remove any residual Wash Buffer.
Transfer the purification column to a clean 1.5 mL collection tube.
Add 15 μL of nuclease-free water to the center of the purification column filter.
Centrifuge for 60 seconds at 14,000 × g to elute the sgRNA.
Check the concentration of the sgRNA with NanoDrop or Qubit.
Make 4 μg aliquots for each sgRNA with PCR tubes.
Freeze the aliquots at -80°C.
Prepare iPSCs for nucleofection by growing 1 million iPSCs.
Maintain the growth of iPSCs as control in the cell sorting step.
Prepare Matrigel-coated wells for seeding nucleofected cells.
Assemble the Cas9/sgRNA ribonuclease protein complex in vitro (Tube 1).
Prepare donor plasmids (Tube 2).
Incubate tubes at 20°C–25°C for 15–20 min.
Harvest cells by following steps 6c–6f.
Count and aliquot 1 million cells into one 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the 1 million cells at 200 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C.
Remove Matrigel from the 6-well plate.
Add 1 mL of prepared mTeSR1 medium with Rock inhibitor to each well.
Remove supernatant completely from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet carefully with the mixed nucleofection reagents.
Transfer the cell suspension into the nucleofector cuvette using a P200 pipet.
Gently tap the nucleofector cuvette to ensure sample covers the bottom of the cuvette.
Transfer the cuvette with a closed lid to Lonza nucleofector.
Start the nucleofection process using program A-023.
Resuspend the cells in the cuvette with prepared mTeSR1 medium.
Add 1 mL of prepared mTeSR1 medium into the cuvette.
Transfer the cell suspension to Matrigel-coated wells, adding 0.5 mL per well.
Wash the cuvette with 1 mL medium and transfer 0.5 mL to each well.
Gently shake the plate left/right and forward/backward for even seeding.
Incubate the cells in a 37°C / 5% CO2 incubator.
Change the culture medium daily with mTeSR1 medium without Rock inhibitor after 24 hours.
Grow the nucleofected cells for 3–4 days to reach 80%-90% confluency.
Prepare Matrigel coated 96-well plate.
Remove the Matrigel when the coating is done.
Add 150 μL of mTeSR1 medium (with Rock inhibitor and 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin) into each well of the 96-well plate.
Detach nucleofection cells and control cells without nucleofection with Accutase.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer to a concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Sort bi-allelically tagged single cells into the prepared 96-well plate by using BD FACSAria II cell sorter.
Separate cells from debris based on forward scatter area (FSC-A) and side scatter area (SSC-A).
Set a single cell gate using width and area metrics of forward scatter (FSC-W versus FSC-A) and side scatter (SSC-W versus SSC-A).
Set the baseline for EGFP and mCherry signal using control cells without nucleofection.
Switch to the nucleofection cells and set the gate for EGFP and mCherry double positive cells.
Sort EGFP and mCherry double positive cells from nucleofection cells into a 96-well plate, placing 1 cell per well using single cell mode.
Incubate the 96-well plates in a 37°C / 5% CO2 incubator.
Refresh half of the media with 1% Penicillin-Streptomycin every 3 days for the first week using a 200 μL multichannel pipette without disturbing the cells.
Check the clones after one week with a microscope and mark the wells containing only one colony.
After one week, refresh half or whole media every 2 days for another week.
Design genotyping primers to confirm successful bi-allelic tagging for SIN3A.
Validate clones when they reach about 80% confluency (usually takes 2 weeks).
Check labeled clones with a microscope and select those with normal morphology for genotyping.
Prepare Matrigel-coated 24-well plates.
Add 0.5 mL mTeSR1 medium with Rock inhibitor to each well.
Directly scratch the marked wells in a vertical, horizontal, and circular way using a P200 pipet to detach cells in the well.
Pipette up and down gently to mix the cell suspension.
Transfer half of the cell suspension to a prepared 24-well plate for passaging.
Transfer half of the cell suspension to a PCR tube for genomic DNA extraction.
Extract the genomic DNA from the cells in the PCR tube.
Spin down the PCR tube with a mini centrifuge to obtain the cell pellet.
Remove the supernatant from the PCR tube.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 50 μL QuickExtract DNA Extraction Solution.
Incubate the cell suspension at 65°C for 15 minutes.
Incubate the cell suspension at 98°C for 5 minutes.
Incubate the cell suspension at 4°C indefinitely.
Use the lysed solution as a PCR template directly.
Set up the genotyping PCR reaction according to the provided parameters.
Perform amplification using the specified cycling parameters.
Check the PCR product with agarose gel electrophoresis.
Expand the correct clones based on the genotyping PCR and Sanger sequencing results.
Make cryogenic stock for the expanded clones.
Check the expression of fluorescent reporters from bi-allelically tagged clones by flow cytometry.
Collect bi-allelically tagged clones and control cells with Accutase.
Resuspend the collected cells in FACS buffer to a concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Perform flow cytometry analysis using BD LSRFortessa cell analyzer or other suitable flow cytometer.
Set the single cell gate for each fluorescent protein by using control cells.
Extract total RNA from the bi-allelically tagged clone.
Follow the QIAGEN RNeasy Plus Mini Kit protocol for RNA extraction.
Perform reverse-transcription reaction to make cDNA from the extracted total RNA using the iScript cDNA synthesis kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Run qPCR to check the expression of pluripotency markers from both control cell and tagged clone.
Check the genetic stability of bi-allelically tagged clones during cell culture cycle and differentiation.
Thaw the clone from the cryogenic stock made in step 52 by following the specified procedure.
Passage the clone three times.
Check the expression of fluorescent reporters by flow cytometry to ensure stable maintenance during cell culture cycle.
Check the genetic stability of bi-allelically tagged clones during differentiation.
Seed 2 × 10^6 cells of the bi-allelically tagged clone in one Matrigel-coated well in a 6-well plate.
Feed the cells with Pre-differentiation Medium for three days.
Dissociate the pre-differentiated cells using Accutase.
Seed the dissociated cells into Poly-L-Ornithine-coated plates at a density of 1 × 10^6 cells per well in a 6-well plate.
Maintain the differentiation culture for two weeks.
Perform flow cytometry analysis for the differentiated glutamatergic neurons with BD LSRFortessa cell analyzer or other flow cytometry cell analyzer.
Set the single cell gate and baseline of each fluorescent protein using control cells.
